verification_report.summary:
The full conditional gradient reduction is correct. The proof was checked in textual order through 11 structured groups containing 49 deductions, with reference and dependency checks recorded in memory/stw_gradient_reduction_01. No critical errors or gaps were found. The conclusion concerns given smooth solution families and assumes the displayed uniform second-order estimate; it proves neither that estimate nor STW existence.

The accepted C0 and |b| bounds and the exact Gauduchon ansatz agree with stw_czero_01 and gauduchon_volume_adjoint_01. The Liouville theorem is used with precisely the stipulated hypotheses: boundedness, a global Lipschitz bound, distributional P_n(Hv)>=0, and exclusion of positive-definite P_n at every lower C2 touch. Its independent audit stw_cone_liouville_01 was initially pending but completed with verdict correct before this report was written.

The normalized Hodge identification is q(Gamma)=star_gamma(Gamma)/(n-1)!. It sends gamma^(n-1) to gamma, hence to I in a gamma-unitary frame. For a diagonal Hermitian coefficient matrix A, the complementary wedge coefficient is (n-2)! times the sum of all entries except the omitted one; normalization gives P_n(A)=((tr A)I-A)/(n-1). Unitary covariance establishes the full matrix identity. The remaining ansatz term is real-linear in first derivatives with fixed smooth coefficients. The eigenvalues of Q_u are the complementary products of the eigenvalues of eta_u, giving exactly det Q_u=exp((n-1)(F+b)). These formulas also hold when n=2, where the drift vanishes.

Compactness gives gradient maxima and a subsequence of centers in a fixed interior coordinate chart. Uniformly controlled complex linear changes normalize gamma at each center and retain a common chart radius. Scaling by A_j produces domains exhausting C^n. The evaluated metric fields g_j, equivalently A_j^2 times the pullback metrics, converge smoothly locally to I. The scaled functions have uniformly bounded values, |partial v_j|g_j<=1, and |partial v_j(0)|=1. The assumed estimate bounds their mixed complex Hessians. Consequently Delta_E v_j=4 tr H(v_j) is uniformly bounded. Interior Laplacian W2p estimates on nested balls, with p>2n, yield C1 compactness. The limit is globally bounded and Lipschitz, and its derivative at zero still has norm one.

The fixed-coordinate matrix comparison is justified by compatible unitary frames obtained through S_j=g_j^(-1/2), which converge to the Euclidean frame. In these frames the scaled principal term is P_n(S_j H(v_j) S_j/(2pi)); bounded Hessians make its difference from P_n(H(v_j)/(2pi)) uniformly o(1). No frame derivatives are taken. The background contributes O(A_j^(-2)), and the first-order term contributes O(A_j^(-1)). The determinant identity remains exact in these normalized frames; raw coordinate coefficient matrices would instead include a metric determinant factor. Thus the stated comparison and its 1/(2pi) normalization are valid.

The uniform F and b bounds imply det(A_j^(-2)Q_u_j)=A_j^(-2n)exp((n-1)(F_j+b_j))->0 uniformly on compact balls. Positivity of these matrices and the uniformly vanishing error give P_n(Hv)>=0 in distributions. No convergence of determinants of weak Hessians, nor any derivative bound for F, is used.

For a lower C2 test h with P_n(Hh)>0, subtracting delta|z-z0|^2 makes the contact strict while preserving positivity because P_n(I)=I. Uniform convergence supplies interior lower contact points z_j->z0. The minimum gives H(v_j)(z_j)>=Hh(z_j)-delta I. Since P_n preserves positive-semidefinite order, the rescaled matrices are bounded below by cI for a fixed c>0. Their determinants are then at least c^n, contradicting uniform determinant collapse. The argument uses only C2 regularity even though the prose calls the test smooth. It proves exactly the maximality required by the accepted Liouville theorem.

The Liouville conclusion contradicts the nonzero derivative at the origin and proves the uniform gradient bound. Substitution into the assumed estimate gives the uniform complex Hessian bound. The Gauduchon identity is not separately needed by this local rescaling step once the stipulated bounds are available; this is harmless redundancy. No full real C2 estimate, nonlinear regularity theorem, C-subsolution assumption, or existence theorem is silently used.

The comparison attribution matches [Szekelyhidi, Section 6, pp. 25-27](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.02762v3), checked through the required theorem search followed by web fallback and the local source. The source's P-map agrees exactly; Definition 15 distinguishes upper tests in the closed cone from lower tests outside the open cone. Its original equation has no gradient term, so it is used only for comparison. The submitted proof independently establishes the drift decay and the accepted book theorem's hypotheses. All checks and the report were persisted; the book was not edited.
